intended_object: The multiplication map of bimodules P_i ⊗_k e_i Z → Z, x e_i ⊗ e_i y ↦ x e_i y. Here Z is the zigzag algebra of a finite simple graph. This map is the differential of the Khovanov–Seidel / Huerfano–Khovanov braid complex at the vertex i. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, P_i ⊗_k e_i Z is modelled as the left ideal of the enveloping algebra Zᵉ = Z ⊗ Zᵐᵒᵖ generated by the idempotent e_i ⊗ op e_i. That ideal is Z e_i ⊗ op(e_i Z), so it does give P_i ⊗_k e_i Z as a Zᵉ-module.

The definition composes the inclusion of this ideal into Zᵉ with the Zᵉ-linear map u ↦ u • 1 into the bimodule Z, where x ⊗ op y acts by m ↦ x m y. On a pure tensor x e_i ⊗ op(e_i y) this gives x e_i · 1 · e_i y = x e_i y, because e_i is idempotent. The lemma `zigzagBraidEvaluation_tmul` proves exactly this.

So the definition is the multiplication map, and it is a bimodule map (Zᵉ-linear) by construction. It is meant as a specific map attached to the zigzag algebra and a vertex, so being specific does not make it too narrow. Mathlib has no braid complex or zigzag algebra for it to duplicate.
